story.title: 1 Unstoppable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Buy Before It Joins Nvidia in the $5 Trillion Club - The Motley Fool

facts.text: Only three companies currently have a $4 trillion valuation: Nvidia , Apple , and Alphabet .
However, I think this club is about to be a bit more crowded by the time 2028 rolls around.
There are three stocks within striking distance of achieving the $4 trillion mark, and one could reach the entry point as quickly as the end of 2026.
Fortunately for TSMC investors, that's slightly below where it expects to grow.
These three stocks are valued at $3.6 trillion, $2.8 trillion, and $2.2 trillion, respectively.
Wall Street analysts expect it to grow its revenue by 43% for the remainder of this year and a 34% pace next year.
Because TSMC is reasonably valued and isn't dealing with shifting profit margins, investors can assume the stock's growth will be closely tied to the revenue growth.
Keithen Drury has positions in Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Microsoft is only a stone's throw away from $4 trillion right now, a barrier it has crossed in the recent past.
The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Microsoft wasn't one of them.
Nvidia ( NVDA -0.88% ) became the first company to cross the $5 trillion market cap threshold last year, powered by its position at the center of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom.
It fell under that line, but is near $6 trillion in market cap now.
Nvidia sells the GPUs, networking equipment, and software that hyperscalers and developers need to build powerful models.
The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia.
Nvidia is currently the only company in the world valued at more than $5 trillion.
Apple ( AAPL +0.42% ) briefly followed Nvidia into $5 trillion territory before slipping back below that milestone.
Interestingly, Apple's AI opportunity looks different from Nvidia's.

The company doesn't need to dominate AI infrastructure because its enormous installed base of devices gives Apple something resembling a tollbooth through which developers can distribute AI-powered services.
There's another company sitting somewhere between these two models: Alphabet ( GOOGL -0.43% ) ( GOOG -0.43% ) .
That's why I think Alphabet can handily become the next $5 trillion company -- and potentially get there before the end of 2028.
Reaching a $5 trillion valuation requires its market capitalization to increase by only about 19%.
Wall Street's consensus estimates currently call for Alphabet to notch roughly $11.81 in earnings per share (EPS) this year, and expand that to $15 in 2027 and nearly $18 by 2028.
Alphabet stock currently trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23.
This means Alphabet could reach $5 trillion by 2028 without requiring multiple expansion .
I think the competitive landscape is what makes Alphabet stock such a compelling long-term investment, though.
